summary: T-0748 fixed the CHARACTER-validator misattribution (a display_name like 'Bot #1' wrongly surfaced as 'email must be a valid email address'), but its own review (R-2, nit) live-probed the sibling LENGTH-validator class explicitly out of scope: a single-token display_name near the client's DISPLAY_NAME_MAX=256 still trips Keycloak's independent 255-char-per-field firstName/lastName cap (splitDisplayName duplicates an unbroken name into BOTH fields), producing KC 400 messageKey 'error-invalid-length-too-long' — which does NOT contain 'person-name', so isPersonNameCharacterError correctly returns false and the request still fell to the SAME misleading EMAIL_INVALID default T-0748 already fixed for the character class. Fix: admin-port.ts adds isPersonNameLengthError (reuses the existing extractKcFieldErrors parser, T-0748) and throws a new NAME_TOO_LONG code when firstName/lastName fail the length validator, checked alongside (not instead of) isPersonNameCharacterError; every other 400 (genuine bad email, unparseable body, unrelated-field drift, or the character class) is unaffected. user-mgmt.ts maps the new code to an honest Russian 400 message; users-form.js's mapUserError anchors it on 'Отображаемое имя' (same field-anchor mechanism as NAME_INVALID_CHARACTERS).
root_cause: admin-port.ts's createHumanUser 400-branch (post-T-0748) checked ONLY the character-validator class before falling to the EMAIL_INVALID default — it did not know KC's declarative user-profile also independently validates firstName/lastName LENGTH (realm-choros.json: {"length":{"max":255},"person-name-prohibited-characters":{}} on both fields, two separate validators in one JSON object). T-0748 closed the attribution gap for one of the two, leaving the other open to the exact same misattribution class T-0748 itself exists to prevent.
live_proof: docs/tasks/T-0762.spec.md §3 — real KC 25.0.6 (container t-0633-keycloak-1, :8180, choros-registrar client_credentials — the EXACT path createHumanUser itself uses, and the SAME container T-0748's own judge used for the R-2 finding), probed 2026-07-13. Confirmed both live 400 body shapes now parsed: single-object {field,errorMessage} when only ONE of firstName/lastName exceeds 255 chars, {errors:[...]} array when a single-token (no-space) 300-char displayName duplicates into BOTH fields and both exceed the cap simultaneously (splitDisplayName's own documented duplication rule). messageKey is 'error-invalid-length-too-long' with params [field, null, 255] in both shapes — byte-identical to T-0748's own R-2 review finding. A control 201 with an ordinary two-word Cyrillic name was also probed live and cleaned up. No orphan KC user left behind by any of the 3 probes (verified via GET .../users?username=...&exact=true after each — [] in all 3 RED cases).

security_notes: No new attack surface: purely an error-message ATTRIBUTION fix, exactly like T-0748. The underlying create-user authorization gate (authorizeOrgWrite/loadAdminContext/assertOrgObjectAuthority) and the anti-collision LOGIN_RESERVED guard are untouched (diff is strictly additive inside the existing 400-branch and its two neighboring layers).

isPersonNameLengthError only ever READS Keycloak's own response body (via the pre-existing extractKcFieldErrors parser, unchanged) to pick a more specific error CODE — no new trust boundary crossed, no new external input accepted.

Safe-default preserved end-to-end: any 400 body shape neither isPersonNameCharacterError nor isPersonNameLengthError recognizes (empty, unparseable, unrelated field, KC-version drift, genuine bad email) falls through to the EXACT prior EMAIL_INVALID behavior — proven by explicit regression tests at both the admin-port.ts layer (AP-10) and the user-mgmt.ts/DB layer.
follow_ups: Non-blocking, out of this task's scope (mirrors T-0748's own R-2 framing): web/src/screens/users-form.js's DISPLAY_NAME_MAX=256 could be tightened toward KC's 255-per-field boundary for the no-space case to prevent the 400 round-trip entirely on the client — a product/UX call (does the owner ever legitimately need a >255-char single-token name?), not a correctness requirement this task's honest-attribution fix depends on.

Not fixed here (T-0741 §6 / T-0748 §7, unchanged, out of scope): src/core/register.ts (self-registration) does not pass displayName to createHumanUser at all, so neither this class of error nor T-0748's can occur on that path.
judge_attack_surface: Try a KC 400 with a single-token 300-char displayName (both firstName AND lastName over the 255 cap simultaneously, live {errors:[...]} array shape) — must surface NAME_TOO_LONG, not silently prefer/mask via a partial match (AP-10 case 3).

Try a KC 400 mixing a bad email AND an over-length firstName in the same {errors:[...]} array — must still surface NAME_TOO_LONG (length problem not masked by a co-occurring email problem), the mirror of T-0748's own AC-2 for the character class (AP-10 case 4).

Try to make isPersonNameCharacterError and isPersonNameLengthError cross-fire on each other's messageKey — a character error ('error-person-name-invalid-character') must map to NAME_INVALID_CHARACTERS, never NAME_TOO_LONG, and vice versa (AP-10 regression case, DB test regression case, web mapUserError regression case — checked at all three layers).

Try a length error on an unrelated field (e.g. 'username') — the field-equality gate (fe.field === 'firstName' || fe.field === 'lastName') runs BEFORE the substring check, so this cannot false-positive into NAME_TOO_LONG; must fall to EMAIL_INVALID (AP-10 final regression case).

Try mounting the real CreateUserModal, fill Отображаемое имя with 256 identical characters (no space), submit against a mocked NAME_TOO_LONG 400 — must show 'слишком длинное' anchored on Отображаемое имя (aria-invalid=true), Email must stay valid, and the pre-fix misleading email text must be completely absent from the dialog (screen-users.mount.test.jsx new case).

Verify the RED-mutation claims directly: temporarily remove isPersonNameLengthError's call site in admin-port.ts and re-run AP-10 — exactly 4 failures, no others; independently remove/disable the NAME_TOO_LONG branch in user-mgmt.ts and re-run the DB suite solo — exactly 1 failure (falls to 503, not even EMAIL_INVALID, proving the branch is genuinely load-bearing).
friction_events: The DB-integration test file (ci/checks/db/user-mgmt.db.test.ts) is excluded from the root tsconfig's "include":["src"] — tsc --noEmit does not type-check it. Verified the new test compiles and behaves correctly by actually RUNNING it live against PG :55432 (solo, DATABASE_URL set), both pre- and post-mutation.

Live-probing the length-too-long shape against t-0633-keycloak-1 required discovering empirically that a SINGLE over-length field produces the single-object {field,errorMessage} shape while BOTH fields over the cap (single-token displayName duplication) produces the {errors:[...]} array shape — this distinction was not fully spelled out in T-0748's own R-2 review text (which only quoted the single-object shape) but both are now live-confirmed and covered by separate unit tests (AP-10).

Concurrent DB-tier test runs from other in-flight worktree tasks (T-0763, T-0764) sharing the same choros-postgres-1 container extended wall-clock time on the db-tier runs (up to ~5min per solo invocation vs. the usual ~4min) — no correctness impact, all runs used --no-file-parallelism and -t user-mgmt scoping to stay isolated from the other files' test databases.

No git stash used anywhere (forbidden per task rules) — both RED-proof revert/restore cycles used the Edit tool directly (apply mutation -> run -> apply restoration text) with a git diff comparison confirming the restored file was byte-identical to the pre-mutation fix.
